value.rationale: The exact two-step corrupted-state recovery problem captures the natural tension between suppressing outlying residuals and escaping a currently corrupted projection. The one-step worst-start optimum is always uniform sampling, making two updates the first horizon where interior tuning can matter. It has a uniquely optimal interior ratio for minority corruption, a sharp half-corruption boundary, and a rare-contamination power-law improvement of \(p^{4/3}\) over \(p\). This is a motivated complete finite-horizon design classification, not an arbitrary isolated numeric example; its limits are explicitly restricted to a scalar duplicate-row model.
